title: Unrolled, the carved war story on Trajan’s Column would stretch 190 metres

cover.alt: Trajan’s Column in Rome: a tall marble column wrapped in a spiral band of relief carving, topped by a bronze statue, with a medieval brick tower and buildings behind.

body: Trajan’s Column in Rome was dedicated on 12 May 113 to celebrate the emperor Trajan’s wars against the Dacians in 101–102 and 105–106. Instead of a plain shaft, the sculptors wrapped it in one continuous band of relief that winds around it **23 times** and would be about 190 m long laid flat, crowded with roughly 2,500 figures. Battles are in the minority: most scenes show the army setting out, building, making sacrifices and hearing the emperor speak, through to the death of the Dacian king Decebalus. The column itself is hollow, with a spiral staircase climbing inside to a viewing deck at the top.

slides.question: How many steps does the spiral staircase inside the column have?
slides.explanation: 185 steps spiral up inside the shaft, which is built from 20 marble drums of about 32 tons each, to a viewing deck at the top.

slides.heading: The frieze is more than six times as long as the column is tall

slides.alt: Close-up of the marble shaft of Trajan’s Column, showing several turns of the spiral frieze crowded with small carved figures, walls, buildings and trees.
slides.caption: A few turns of the frieze, packed with military and civilian scenes, each band running straight on into the next.
slides.credit: Institute for the Study of the Ancient World · CC BY 2.0

slides.heading: It was not plain marble
slides.text: The figures were carved in shallow relief and detailed with paint and metal fittings. The libraries beside the column apparently had upper viewing platforms, from which people could see them more closely.

slides.question: Whose bronze statue stands on top of Trajan’s Column today?
slides.explanation: Trajan’s own statue vanished in the Middle Ages. On 4 December 1587 Pope Sixtus V had a bronze Saint Peter put up, and it is still there.
